sentences.en: A Hare was one day making fun of a Tortoise for being so slow upon his feet.
sentences.zh: 有一天，一只兔子嘲笑乌龟走路太慢。

sentences.en: "Wait a bit," said the Tortoise; "I'll run a race with you, and I'll wager that I win."
sentences.zh: 「等着瞧吧，」乌龟说，「我跟你赛跑，我还敢打赌我能赢。」

sentences.en: "Oh, well," replied the Hare, who was much amused at the idea, "let's try and see" …
sentences.zh: 「哦，好啊，」兔子觉得这主意十分可笑，答道，「那就试试看吧……」

sentences.en: … and it was soon agreed that the fox should set a course for them, and be the judge.
sentences.zh: ……很快便商定由狐狸给他们划定赛道，并当裁判。

sentences.en: When the time came both started off together, but the Hare was soon so far ahead that he thought he might as well have a rest …
sentences.zh: 比赛开始时两个一同出发，可兔子很快就跑得远远领先，觉得不妨歇一歇……

sentences.en: … so down he lay and fell fast asleep.
sentences.zh: ……于是躺下便睡熟了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile the Tortoise kept plodding on, and in time reached the goal.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，乌龟一直艰难而稳步地走，终于到了终点。

sentences.en: At last the Hare woke up with a start, and dashed on at his fastest, but only to find that the Tortoise had already won the race.
sentences.zh: 最后兔子猛地醒来，以最快的速度冲出去，却发现乌龟早已赢了比赛。

sentences.en: Slow and steady wins the race.
sentences.zh: 稳扎稳打，方能取胜。

sentences.en: A Soldier gave his Horse a plentiful supply of oats in time of war, and tended him with the utmost care …
sentences.zh: 战争时期，一名士兵给他的马充足的燕麦，照料得极为精心……

sentences.en: … for he wished him to be strong to endure the hardships of the field …
sentences.zh: ……因为他希望它强壮得能熬住战场的艰苦……

sentences.en: … and swift to bear his master, when need arose, out of the reach of danger.
sentences.zh: ……并在需要时迅速把主人带离险境。

sentences.en: But when the war was over he employed him on all sorts of drudgery, bestowing but little attention upon him …
sentences.zh: 可战争一结束，他便让马干各种粗活，很少再过问它……

sentences.en: … and giving him, moreover, nothing but chaff to eat.
sentences.zh: ……而且只给它谷壳吃。

sentences.en: The time came when war broke out again, and the Soldier saddled and bridled his Horse, and, having put on his heavy coat of mail, mounted …
sentences.zh: 战事又起的日子到了，士兵给马配上鞍辔，穿上沉重的铠甲，跨上……

sentences.en: … him to ride off and take the field.
sentences.zh: 「……马背，要骑它上阵。

sentences.en: But the poor half-starved beast sank down under his weight, and said to his rider, "You will have to go into battle on foot this time.
sentences.zh: 可这头饿得半死的可怜牲口在他身下瘫倒了，对骑手说：「这一回你只好步行上阵了。

sentences.en: Thanks to hard work and bad food, you have turned me from a Horse into an ass …
sentences.zh: 多亏重活和劣食，你已把我从一匹马变成了一头驴……」

sentences.en: … and you cannot in a moment turn me back again into a Horse."
sentences.zh: 「……而你不能一下子又把我变回马去。」

sentences.en: Once upon a time the Oxen determined to be revenged upon the Butchers for the havoc they wrought in their ranks …
sentences.zh: 从前，公牛们决定向屠夫报仇，因为屠夫在它们中间大肆杀戳……

sentences.en: … and plotted to put them to death on a given day.
sentences.zh: ……并密谋在约定的日子把他们弄死。

sentences.en: They were all gathered together discussing how best to carry out the plan …
sentences.zh: 它们聚在一起商议怎样最好地施行这个计划……

sentences.en: … and the more violent of them were engaged in sharpening their horns for the fray …
sentences.zh: ……其中较激烈的一些已在磨角，准备厮杀……

sentences.en: … when an old Ox got up upon his feet and said, "My brothers, you have good reason, I know, to hate these Butchers, but, at any rate …
sentences.zh: ……这时一头老公牛站起来说：「弟兄们，我知道你们恨这些屠夫有理，可无论如何……」

sentences.en: … they understand their trade and do what they have to do without causing unnecessary pain.
sentences.zh: 「……他们懂本行，该做的事做得干净，不叫人多受无谓的痛苦。

sentences.en: But if we kill them, others, who have no experience, will be set to slaughter us …
sentences.zh: 可我们若杀了他们，派来宰我们的就是些没经验的生手……」

sentences.en: … and will by their bungling inflict great sufferings upon us.
sentences.zh: 「……他们会因笨拙而给我们带来极大的苦楚。

sentences.en: For you may be sure that, even though all the Butchers perish, mankind will never go without their beef."
sentences.zh: 你们尽可放心，即便屠夫全死光了，人类也绝不会吃不上牛肉。」
